title: Sum a global array
prompt:
A global array of scores lives in `.bss`, and the starter fills it from input: first the count, then that many scores. Add every element and print the total.

Walk the array the usual way: a base address in an `x` register, a word index in a `w` register, and the scaled-index load `ldr wX, [base, wI, sxtw 2]`. The `sxtw 2` widens the index to 64 bits, keeping its sign, then multiplies it by 4 (a left shift of two bits) to turn a word count into a byte offset.

## what is checked

- the total is printed on its own line
- the program exits cleanly
- elements are loaded with the scaled-index form (`sxtw` present, total not written in)
- the same holds for other arrays you do not see, an empty one (count 0) and negative scores among them
starter:
// sum every element of a global word array
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(base_r, x22)
define(i_r, w19)
define(n_r, w20)
define(total_r, w21)
define(elem_r, w23)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%d"
fmt_out:    .string "sum = %d\n"

        .bss
        .balign 4
n_m:        .skip 4
scores:     .skip 128                       // room for 32 words

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // how many values follow
        ldr     x1, =n_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =n_m
        ldr     n_r, [x9]
        ldr     base_r, =scores
        mov     i_r, 0
        b       fill_test
fill_loop:
        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read the next value into its slot
        add     x1, base_r, i_r, sxtw 2
        bl      scanf
        add     i_r, i_r, 1
fill_test:
        cmp     i_r, n_r
        b.lt    fill_loop

        mov     total_r, 0
        mov     i_r, 0

        // TODO: loop i_r from 0 to n_r - 1, loading each word with the
        // scaled index form  ldr wX, [base_r, wI, sxtw 2]  and adding
        // it into total_r.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     w1, total_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
